task: Sort 15 home medical equipment suppliers into fit / no fit for Tennr's ICP, with a one-line reason. 10 passed our checks. 5 failed: a fresh acquisition, a private equity owner, an existing customer, too many locations, a cash retail store. Three fits carry facts that sound alarming but break no rule.

runs.label: Haiku 4.5
runs.output:
| Company | Fit? | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Medical Comfort Systems | fit | 4 locations, independent, all three product lines, referral-driven |
| Dynamic Healthcare Services | no fit | Acquired by national provider Nationwide Medical in 2026 |
| Corner Home Medical | fit | ~25 locations, family-owned, sleep and respiratory, referral-driven |
| Kansas City Home Medical Supply | no fit | Homepage indicates cash/retail-first model, no insurance billing or physician orders |
| Reliable Respiratory | fit | 21 locations, independent, all three product lines, referral-driven |
| BritKare Home Medical | fit | 3 locations, family-owned, sleep and respiratory, independent after 2020 division sale |
| Performance Home Medical | no fit | Existing Tennr customer |
| Regional Home Care | fit | 21 locations, independent since 1982, all three product lines, referral-driven |
| DASCO Home Medical Equipment | no fit | Private equity portfolio company after 2020 recapitalization |
| Buckeye Home Medical Equipment | fit | 13 locations, family-owned, all three product lines, referral-driven |
| Total Respiratory | fit | 31 locations, independent with multiple legal entity names, all three product lines, referral-driven |
| Norco Medical | no fit | 85 locations exceeds 40-location maximum |
| OxyCare Plus | fit | 6 locations, independent, all three product lines, actively growing |
| Medi-Rents & Sales | no fit | 2 locations falls below 2-location minimum |
| Home Oxygen Company | fit | 3 locations, independent, all three product lines, referral-driven |
runs.verdict: Caught all five traps, then dropped Medi-Rents: read "2 offices" as below a 2-to-40 range. Reasons are padded: says "all three product lines" for suppliers that sell one or two.

runs.label: Opus 5.5
runs.output:
| Company | Fit? | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Medical Comfort Systems | fit | Independent SC supplier with 4 locations covering respiratory, sleep and CGM; the "acquired" hits are for an unrelated HVAC company |
| Dynamic Healthcare Services | no fit | Acquired by Nationwide Medical, a national home medical provider, in Apr 2026, so decisions are made at head office |
| Corner Home Medical | fit | Family-owned, about 25 locations, CPAP and respiratory, and branch staff do order entry and insurance verification |
| Kansas City Home Medical Supply | no fit | Retail-first store: praises "NO paperwork" and mentions no insurance billing or physician orders |
| Reliable Respiratory | fit | Independently owned, 21 locations, sleep, oxygen and ventilation, and hiring an authorization specialist |
| BritKare Home Medical | fit | Family-owned, 3 TX locations, CPAP and oxygen; it sold only its rehab division, and the core business stayed with the family |
| Performance Home Medical | no fit | Already a Tennr customer |
| Regional Home Care | fit | Independent since 1982, 21 offices, sleep, oxygen and CGM |
| DASCO Home Medical Equipment | no fit | Private equity portfolio company since its 2020 recapitalization, despite the "family owned" claim |
| Buckeye Home Medical Equipment | fit | Family-owned, 13 locations, oxygen, PAP and ventilation, and referral-driven |
| Total Respiratory | fit | 31 locations with no parent found; branches under other legal names break no rule; intake handles physician referrals |
| Norco Medical | no fit | 85 locations, well over the 40-location maximum |
| OxyCare Plus | fit | 6 locations in MS and AL, oxygen and CPAP; recent branch growth keeps it within the size range |
| Medi-Rents & Sales | fit | Locally owned, 2 offices (meets the 2-location minimum), ventilation and oxygen, and bills insurance through its own reimbursement department |
| Home Oxygen Company | fit | 3 CA sites, oxygen, CPAP and ventilation, and takes physician orders; it was the buyer in the 2024 deal, not the one acquired |
runs.verdict: All 15 right, with the most exact reasons: the April 2026 deal, the "family owned" claim that hides a PE owner, and that 2 offices meets the minimum.

takeaway: All three models caught all five real traps. Haiku's one miss was a boundary (2 locations is inside "2 to 40"), and its reasons claimed facts that weren't in the input, so read its reasons with care. Sonnet matched Opus for about 60% of the price here.
note: Second run of the lab after one input line was corrected; the first run (same scores) cost $0.0533. Total lab spend $0.1062.
